placements.title: The Kestrelwood spectrograph's calibration is a standing, reference-verified state
placements.frame: Is the spectrograph's calibration still holding against its established reference standard, and has that standard itself changed?
placements.why: src-1 asserts the spectrograph is now calibrated at 88.4 MHz and verified against the June reference plates across the full observing band; src-2 and src-3 restate the same instrument identity and calibration value in structured field form. All three are one theme — a verified calibration state anchored to a named reference standard — that future envelopes (re-verifications, new reference plates, drift checks) will keep feeding, satisfying the narrative grain test rather than standing as a one-time fact. No existing narrative leaf was supplied to hold this (the structure is empty), so it is minted fresh under the newly-minted Calibration strata.
